html:
Tŝilhqot'in Nen is the land of the Tsilhqot'in, an Athabaskan people of the Chilcotin plateau in central British Columbia, between the Fraser River and the Coast Mountains. They lived from salmon, deer and roots, and traded with the Nuxalk on the coast and the Secwepemc to the east.

In 1864, after smallpox had killed many of them and road builders threatened their land, Tsilhqot'in warriors killed a road crew and others in what became known as the Chilcotin War. Five chiefs who came to talk peace were hanged. In 2018 the government of Canada said they had been innocent.

In 2014 the Supreme Court of Canada, in Tsilhqot'in Nation v. British Columbia, recognised their Aboriginal title to about 1,750 square kilometres. It was the first time a Canadian court declared that a First Nation held title to a specific area of land.
